title: Counting Sidon Sets
description: Let f(N) be the max Sidon subset size and A(N) the number of Sidon subsets of {1,...,N}. Is A(N)/2^{f(N)} → ∞? (Yes) Is A(N) = 2^{(1+o(1))f(N)}? (No)

meta.author: Paul Erdős, Peter Cameron
originalContributions: Lean formalization of Sidon set definition
Saxton-Thomason and KLRS bounds as axioms
meta.assumptions: 4 axioms: cameron_erdos_q1_true, cameron_erdos_q2_false, saxton_thomason_lower_bound, klrs_upper_bound. 0 sorries.

overview.historicalContext: This problem, posed by Cameron and Erdős, asks about counting Sidon sets (sets where all pairwise sums are distinct). It connects to additive combinatorics and the hypergraph container method. The problem appears as C9 in Guy's 'Unsolved Problems in Number Theory'. Sidon sets — also called B₂ sequences — were introduced by Simon Sidon in the 1930s in the context of Fourier analysis; Erdős and Turán proved in 1941 that the maximum Sidon subset of {1, …, N} has size ~√N, and constructions achieving this via Singer difference sets in finite fields were known by the 1940s. Cameron and Erdős posed their counting question in the early 1990s, anticipating that the exponential structure of 2^{f(N)} subsets would need to be understood more precisely. The 2015 resolution using the hypergraph container method of Balogh-Morris-Samotij and independently Saxton-Thomason represented a major breakthrough in counting sparse combinatorial structures.
overview.problemStatement: Let f(N) be the size of the largest Sidon subset of {1,...,N} and A(N) the number of Sidon subsets. Question 1: Is A(N)/2^{f(N)} → ∞? Question 2: Is A(N) = 2^{(1+o(1))f(N)}?
overview.text: Let f(N) be the max Sidon subset size and A(N) the number of Sidon subsets of {1,...,N}. Is A(N)/2^{f(N)} → ∞? (Yes) Is A(N) = 2^{(1+o(1))f(N)}? (No)
overview.proofStrategy: The formalization defines Sidon sets and the counting functions, then states the Cameron-Erdős questions and their answers as axioms. The current best bounds (Saxton-Thomason lower, KLRS upper) are included.
keyInsights: A Sidon set (B₂ sequence) has all pairwise sums distinct: $a + b = c + d \implies \{a,b\} = \{c,d\}$
The maximum Sidon subset of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ has size $f(N) \sim \sqrt{N}$ (Erdős-Turán 1941)
Question 2: NO — the exponent is between 1.16 and 6.442, not $1 + o(1)$
The hypergraph container method (Balogh-Morris-Samotij, Saxton-Thomason 2015) was the key breakthrough for counting sparse structures

sections.mathContext: $\text{IsSidon}(S) \iff \forall a \le b,\, c \le d \in S: a + b = c + d \implies (a = c \wedge b = d)$. All pairwise sums are distinct (B$_2$ sequence). Includes `IsSidon'` (pair-set form) and `sidon_equiv` proving the two definitions agree.

sections.title: Known Asymptotic
sections.summary: Documents Erdős-Turán f(N) ~ √N (in docstring) and states `SidonSizeConjecture` for the refined bound
sections.mathContext: $f(N) \sim \sqrt{N}$ as $N \to \infty$ (Erdős-Turán, recorded only in docstring; not formally stated as a theorem). `SidonSizeConjecture` formalizes the refined statement $f(N) = \sqrt{N} + O(N^\varepsilon)$ for any $\varepsilon > 0$.

sections.title: Cameron-Erdős Question 1
sections.summary: Is A(N)/2^{f(N)} → ∞? (Answer: Yes; declared as axiom `cameron_erdos_q1_true`)
sections.mathContext: Q1: Is $A(N) / 2^{f(N)} \to \infty$? *YES*. The Saxton-Thomason bound $A(N) \ge 2^{1.16 f(N)}$ implies $A(N)/2^{f(N)} \ge 2^{0.16 f(N)} \to \infty$.

sections.title: Cameron-Erdős Question 2
sections.summary: Is A(N) = 2^{(1+o(1))f(N)}? (Answer: No; declared as axiom `cameron_erdos_q2_false`)
sections.mathContext: Q2: Is $A(N) = 2^{(1+o(1))f(N)}$? *NO*. The bounds $2^{1.16 f(N)} \le A(N) \le 2^{6.442 f(N)}$ show the exponent is not $1 + o(1)$.

sections.title: Current Best Bounds
sections.summary: Saxton-Thomason lower and KLRS upper bound axioms, combined into `current_bounds` theorem
sections.mathContext: $2^{1.16 f(N)} \le A(N) \le 2^{6.442 f(N)}$ for large $N$. Lower: Saxton-Thomason (2015, hypergraph containers). Upper: Kohayakawa-Lee-Rödl-Samotij (2015).

sections.title: Summary
sections.summary: Main results bundled: `erdos_861_summary` and `erdos_861` combine Q1-true and Q2-false axioms
sections.mathContext: $A(N)/2^{f(N)} \to \infty$ (Q1: YES) and $\exists c \in [1.16, 6.442]: A(N) = 2^{(c+o(1))f(N)}$ (Q2: NO, exponent $\neq 1$). The exact $c$ remains open.

conclusion.summary: Erdős Problem #861 (Cameron-Erdős problem on counting Sidon sets) is solved. Question 1 is answered YES (A(N)/2^{f(N)} → ∞). Question 2 is answered NO (the exponent is between 1.16 and 6.442, not 1+o(1)).
conclusion.implications: The hypergraph container method (Saxton-Thomason) provides powerful tools for counting combinatorial structures. The gap between bounds [1.16, 6.442] remains to be tightened.
openQuestions: What is the exact constant c such that A(N) = 2^{(c+o(1))f(N)}?
Can the bounds be improved beyond [1.16, 6.442]?
Does f(N) = √N + O(N^ε) hold for all ε > 0?
